sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 3706.4 ± 392 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by confocal imaging in HEK 293T cells; co-localization with β-arrestin 1 observed upon receptor activation. No quantitative receptor function assay (e.g., calcium flux, ERK phosphorylation) reported for the tagged construct specifically.
sites.rationale: L2 and L3 together report a full-length, membrane-anchored zebrafish S1p2 construct with an N-terminal HA tag that reaches the cell surface in HEK 293T cells. Zebrafish S1p2 is the direct ortholog of human S1PR2; the N-terminal extracellular domain is conserved in topology. Human S1PR2 carries no signal peptide (raw topology begins with 'O'), so a tag prepended before M1 is not cleaved and remains extracellular. The sole extracellular terminus of this GPCR is the N-terminus (residues 1–34), making insert_after_residue=0 the unique topology-derived junction. Position is indirect (ortholog) and no residue number is cited, so position_evidence is topology_derived. Zebrafish S1p2 (close ortholog of human S1PR2) was cloned full-length into pCS2+ with an HA tag at the N-terminus and expressed in HEK 293T cells. Confocal imaging (L3) confirmed surface display of the HA-tagged receptor co-localizing with flag-tagged β-arrestin 1. No residue number is named; the tag is at the N-terminus. Human S1PR2 has no signal peptide (topology begins with extracellular residues 1–34), so the N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0, before M1) places the tag on the extracellular face. TM1 begins at residue 35, giving 34 residues of extracellular buffer.

sources.claim: Zebrafish S1p2 was amplified from cDNA of 24 hpf (hours postfertilization) zebrafish embryos and cloned into pCS2+ via ClaI and StuI restriction sites with a HA tag at the N-terminus of S1p2.

literature_notes: L1 reports a C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length human S1PR2 in pEG-BacMam. The C-terminus falls within the intracellular span 291–353 (computed landmarks), so this tag is cytoplasmic and is recorded in other_positions rather than sites. L2 and L3 are the only ledger lines supporting an extracellular tag site; they ground a single N-terminal prepend site via the zebrafish ortholog. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion (ECL1 92–108, ECL2 169–189, ECL3 256–269) for S1PR2 or a close ortholog, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length human S1PR2 (pEG-BacMam); residue 353 (V) lies within the intracellular C-terminal tail (computed span 291–353), so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface-display site.
